page0.text: How long has it taken for her to notice something is wrong?

page1.text:
She wakes from a strange premonition of a spider's web and makes her way to the hallway.
"...Shirou?"
At first, she thinks that it might be coming from her Master.
The abnormality came from Shirou Emiya's room before snaking outside.

page2.text:
"...What a bother. Is he still doing magecraft training?"
Saber sighs, her golden hair swaying.
It's good that he's enthusiastic but his body won't last unless he rests.
And when she decides to go warn him, she realizes her own mistake.

page3.text:
...
She confirms her suspicions and gasps.
The abnormality isn't coming from Shirou's room.
Under the moonlight.
A string, thin as her hair, runs through the darkness.

page4.text:
The single string goes into Shirou's room from outside the house.
It's so thin that even the Bounded Field here didn't catch wind of it.

page5.text:
...
There's no time.
She transforms into an armored knight and swiftly heads out.

page6.text:
Her feet run through the quiet streets.
Nothing will stop her.
She knows where she must go.
She only has to follow the string, the pulse of her Master.
All she can do is run as fast as she can.
It makes no difference whether her destination is her enemy's territory, nor how many death traps await her.
She has sworn to protect her Master.
Anything that might come is negligible.

page7.text:
...
A mountain contaminated with an abundance of magical energy.
Ghosts fly around in the sky like crows,
and the leaves in the trees are covered in unseen blood.
Within the collected magical energy reside these stripped-down souls, and the stark mountainside will consume those that approach.
If there is a place in this world where death is assured, this is unmistakably the perfect example.

page8.text:
...
She enters without hesitation.
Such things will not stop her.
If this place is hell, then she has to save her Master all the more.
She runs up the stone stairs.
The expected traps and obstacles do not manifest.
The mountain gate is already in her sight, and she should reach it with one more step of her magical energy-infused legs.
...
But, her advance ends.
No... It is halted by an enemy.

page9.text:
Atop a staircase landing, beneath the eaves of the mountain gate...
There stands one Servant.
His name is Sasaki Kojirou.
The Assassin-class Servant, the protector of Ryudou Temple, wields the longsword Monohoshizao.

page10.text:
...
Her mind in unrest, Saber readies Invisible Air.
Her Master is on the other side of the mountain gate.
But the identity of the Servant that stands before her is too much of an unknown.
The way he revealed his identity with no hesitation...
He does not take a stance and his hostility seems transparent, pure.

page11.text:
...
She cannot grasp his strength from such a transparent offering.
She can see his power as a Servant.
Assassin is not powerful, so it ought to be easy to maneuver and defeat him. But her instincts tell her otherwise.
They tell her that in a duel, she will not best him.

page12.text:
"...I do not have any business with you. Move out of the way, Assassin."
Saber clamps down on her anxiety and glares at Assassin.
...There's only one step until she can strike the opponent.
To move up or down...
The moment one of them makes a move, the other will strike with a killing blow.

page13.text:
"Did you not hear me? I said to move, Assassin."
Her final warning.
The longsword-wielding swordsman accepts with grace and poise.
"...Yes, I see. You wish to pass the mountain gate?"
...
Her green eyes would but pierce his body for such a foolish question.
He must like her reaction.
The longsword weaves through the night in an arc.
"Then force your way through. If you do not hurry, your Master's life will be forfeit."
He laughs with the same cool, collected tone.
"Assassin...!"
Saber steps up in reply.
The longsword swiftly strikes, and Saber's invisible blade intercedes.

page14.text:
The sounds of the clashing swords echo through the breezy mountaintop.
Their skill seems equal.
But she has no advantage.
"Khh..."
Frustration builds.
The enemy that she must defeat quickly is actually skilled and a great hindrance.

page15.text:
"Shirou, please...!"
She grits her teeth and prays with all her might.
In that moment, excessive thoughts beyond the duel seep into her skull.
The battle does not end.
The mountain gate is too far away.
